content:
olivia: quick q — i'm about to land a tf change to add a new gpu nodepool for inference (h100-heavy). trying to get the reservation/spot fallback right, and also how we wire the instance-profile secret. pinging for a quick preflight.

raj: thanks for the heads up. can you paste the relevant snippet? curious how you plan to attach the capacityReservation and the spot fallback taints.

olivia: sure — here's the plan (simplified):
```hcl
resource "aws_eks_node_group" "inference_h100" {
  instance_types = ["p4de.24xlarge", "p4d.24xlarge"]
  capacity_reservation_specification {
    capacity_reservation_preference = "open"
    capacity_reservation_target {
      capacity_reservation_id = var.cap_res_id
    }
  }
  scaling_config { desired_size = 10 }
  labels = { "node.kubernetes.io/instance-type" = "h100-inference" }
  taints = ["dedicated=inference:NoSchedule"]
}

# spot fallback handled by separate nodegroup with taint + nodeSelector in workloads
```

olivia: also need to mount the instance-profile secret (role-creds) via k8s secret; current plan is to generate secret in infra pipeline and reference it in the nodegroup user-data bootstrap script. is that okay?

kevin: couple of things — (1) capacity reservations on h100 SKUs are region/az specific, make sure var.cap_res_id is AZ-scoped, (2) mixing p4de/p4d is ok but verify kernel+drivers image compatibility, we've hit mismatches before, (3) prefer using IAM instance profile attached to node role rather than writing creds into k8s secret if possible.

maria: fwiw for spot fallback we usually create a smaller spot nodegroup with the same labels but `spot=true` taint, plus a cluster-autoscaler profile. then workloads use PodTopologySpread + tolerations. keeps reserved pool clean.

raj: +1 on avoiding plaintext creds. if the pipeline must create a k8s secret, restrict it to the bootstrap phase and rotate ASAP. also check ssh/key distribution for the image.

olivia: noted — i'll switch to instance-profile approach. one weirdness: when we tried capacity reservations earlier the kubelet tags didn't map to `capacityReservationId` metadata so internal autoscaler couldn't prefer reserved nodes. has anyone seen that?

kevin: i have. the aws provider sets the CR on the EC2 instance but kubelet/node labels won't reflect it automatically. we added a small controller that watches EC2 tags and reconciles a node label `reserved=true`. it's in infra-utils repo (tag: ec2-reservation-watcher).

olivia: do you remember if that controller needs any extra IAM perms?

kevin: minimal — DescribeInstances, DescribeTags, and node label patching (k8s api access via a service account). i can paste the policy.

infra-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-infra/terraform/compare/.../gpu-h100-nodepool — olivia (draft)

maria: i'll take a look at the PR this afternoon. two quick asks: add a tf var for `max_spot_price` (we capped before), and a note in CHANGELOG about the AZ reservation mapping.

olivia: thanks — adding both now. also adding a post-deploy smoke job that runs a tiny inference pod to validate kernels + cuda.

raj: one last thing — can you mark the nodegroup with label `redwood.infra/critical=true` so our SRE oncall runbooks prioritize it?

olivia: will do. thanks everyone — i'll land the PR once i switch to instance-profile wiring and add the watcher reference + smoke job. will ping here when it's live. :rocket:
